mcqs.question: Which of the following correctly lists the metals in order of decreasing reactivity according to the reactivity series?

options.A: K > Na > Ca > Mg > Al > Zn > Fe > Ni > Sn > Pb > H > Cu > Ag > Au
options.B: Na > K > Ca > Mg > Al > Zn > Fe > Ni > Sn > Pb > H > Cu > Ag > Au
options.C: K > Ca > Na > Mg > Al > Zn > Fe > Ni > Sn > Pb > H > Cu > Ag > Au
options.D: K > Na > Mg > Ca > Al > Zn > Fe > Ni > Sn > Pb > H > Cu > Ag > Au

mcqs.answer: K > Na > Ca > Mg > Al > Zn > Fe > Ni > Sn > Pb > H > Cu > Ag > Au
mcqs.explanation: Option A follows the standard NCERT reactivity series from the most reactive metal (potassium) to the least reactive (gold). The other options have metals placed out of order, violating the established series.

mcqs.question: A strip of zinc metal is placed in a solution of copper(II) sulfate. Which of the following best predicts the outcome?

options.A: No reaction occurs because zinc is less reactive than copper.
options.B: Zinc displaces copper, forming zinc sulfate and copper metal precipitates.
options.C: Copper displaces zinc, forming copper metal and zinc sulfate.
options.D: Both metals dissolve forming a mixture of ions.

mcqs.answer: Zinc displaces copper, forming zinc sulfate and copper metal precipitates.
mcqs.explanation: Zinc is higher than copper in the reactivity series, so it can displace copper from its salt. The reaction is Zn + CuSO₄ → ZnSO₄ + Cu(s). Options A and C reverse the direction, and D is not a displacement reaction.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand reactions of metals with salt solutions
mcqs.question: When iron metal is placed in copper(II) sulfate solution, which statement correctly describes the reaction?

options.A: Iron is displaced by copper, producing copper metal and iron sulfate.
options.B: No reaction occurs because iron is less reactive than copper.
options.C: Iron displaces copper, producing iron(II) sulfate and copper metal.
options.D: Both metals form a complex ion without any displacement.

mcqs.answer: Iron displaces copper, producing iron(II) sulfate and copper metal.
mcqs.explanation: Iron lies above copper in the reactivity series, so it can displace copper from its salt: Fe + CuSO₄ → FeSO₄ + Cu(s). Option B is wrong because iron is actually more reactive than copper. Options A and D describe incorrect processes.

mcqs.question: According to the reactivity series, which metal is more reactive?
mcqs.explanation: The series lists magnesium above zinc (… Ca > Mg > Al > Zn …), indicating magnesium is more reactive. Therefore it can displace zinc from its compounds, while zinc cannot displace magnesium.

mcqs.question: Identify the option that correctly represents the reactivity series (most to least reactive).

options.A: K > Na > Ca > Mg > Al > Zn > Fe > Ni > Sn > Pb > H > Cu > Ag > Au
options.B: K > Na > Mg > Ca > Al > Zn > Fe > Ni > Sn > Pb > H > Cu > Ag > Au
options.C: Na > K > Ca > Mg > Al > Zn > Fe > Ni > Sn > Pb > H > Cu > Ag > Au
options.D: K > Na > Ca > Mg > Al > Fe > Zn > Ni > Sn > Pb > H > Cu > Ag > Au

mcqs.answer: K > Na > Ca > Mg > Al > Zn > Fe > Ni > Sn > Pb > H > Cu > Ag > Au
mcqs.explanation: Option A follows the standard NCERT ordering. Options B, C, and D each place at least one metal out of its correct position, violating the established series.

mcqs.question: A piece of aluminium metal is placed in a solution of silver nitrate. Which set of products will be formed?

options.A: No reaction occurs because aluminium is less reactive than silver.
options.B: Aluminium displaces silver, forming aluminium nitrate and silver metal.
options.C: Silver displaces aluminium, forming silver nitrate and aluminium metal.
options.D: Both metals precipitate as a mixed hydroxide.

mcqs.answer: Aluminium displaces silver, forming aluminium nitrate and silver metal.
mcqs.explanation: Aluminium is higher than silver in the reactivity series, so it can displace silver: Al + 3AgNO₃ → Al(NO₃)₃ + 3Ag(s). Option A is incorrect because aluminium is more reactive. Options C and D describe impossible processes in this context.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand reactions of metals with salt solutions
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is a common misconception about metal reactions with water?

options.A: Metals above hydrogen in the reactivity series can displace hydrogen from water.
options.B: All metals, regardless of reactivity, can displace hydrogen from water.
options.C: Metals below hydrogen cannot react with acids.

mcqs.answer: All metals, regardless of reactivity, can displace hydrogen from water.
mcqs.explanation: The misconception is that every metal can liberate hydrogen from water. In reality, only metals placed above hydrogen in the series (e.g., Na, K, Ca, Mg) can do so; many metals (e.g., Cu, Ag) do not react with water. Option A is a correct statement, C is also correct, and D is therefore wrong.

mcqs.question: Given the reactivity series K > Na > Ca > Mg > Al > Zn > Fe > …, which pair correctly shows a metal that can displace the other from its salt solution?

options.A: Zinc will displace iron from iron(II) sulfate solution.
options.B: Iron will displace zinc from zinc sulfate solution.
options.C: Magnesium will displace calcium from calcium nitrate solution.
options.D: Calcium will displace magnesium from magnesium chloride solution.

mcqs.answer: Iron will displace zinc from zinc sulfate solution.
mcqs.explanation: A more reactive metal can displace a less reactive one. Iron is higher than zinc in the series, so it can displace zinc (Fe + ZnSO₄ → FeSO₄ + Zn). Option A reverses the direction, C is wrong because calcium is more reactive than magnesium, and D is also reversed.
